name: Discord
description: Community chat platform with servers (guilds), channels, voice, and a rich bot/app platform.
access_notes: Anyone can create an app for free in the Discord Developer Portal and generate a bot token immediately. OAuth2 (authorization code) is used to install apps to servers/users and to get user bearer tokens. Scaling caveat: privileged intents (e.g. message content) and bot verification are required once a bot exceeds ~100 servers, but small-scale/production use is fully self-serve.
mcp_notes: Composio catalog lists both a 'Discord' (OAuth2) and a 'Discord Bot' (165 tools) toolkit. Discord ships no first-party MCP server; ecosystem is community implementations (e.g. discord-agent-mcp, @pasympa/discord-mcp) plus Anthropic's narrow official Discord plugin for Claude Code.
uncertainty_notes: Bot token is a static token sent as 'Authorization: Bot <token>' — recorded as api_key since it is a long-lived generated credential rather than an OAuth-issued bearer token. Gateway (websocket) needed for real-time events; interaction webhooks and incoming webhooks cover HTTP push.

evidence.note: 'Authenticating with the Discord API can be done in one of two ways: bot token ... or an OAuth2 bearer token'; REST API at discord.com/api/v10.
'Discord uses OAuth2 as the standard authorization framework'; bot tokens used for Gateway connections and most REST calls.
Self-serve app creation and bot token generation in the Developer Portal; covers gateway intents and interaction endpoints (HTTP webhooks) for receiving events.
Catalog lists 'Discord' (DISCORD, 28 tools, OAUTH2) and 'Discord Bot' (DISCORDBOT, 165 tools) toolkits.
